input_signals.name: Liquid Sales Bargain
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High sales-to-price firms outperform when their apparent cheapness is supported by a strong net working-capital position.
input_signals.reasoning: Sales yield captures inexpensive operating scale but does not reveal whether near-term obligations can be funded. Interacting it with asset-scaled net working capital favors liquid value firms and downweights sales-rich businesses facing acute payment pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liability-Financed Cash Adjustment
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, MAX(DELTA(lt, 1), SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating-cash-flow yield predicts higher returns when the reported cash generation is not accompanied by an expansion of total liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Rising liabilities can support cash flow through supplier credit, deferred obligations, or new borrowing, making an apparently high cash yield less reassuring. Deducting only positive liability accumulation directly addresses the prior cash-yield signal’s weak portfolio evidence without imposing a retained-earnings main effect.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, max( delta( lt, 1 ), sub( at, at ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Accumulated-Deficit Adjusted Book Value
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ceq, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), MAX(NEG(re), SUB(at, at)))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Book-equity cheapness predicts higher returns after imposing a continuous valuation penalty for accumulated deficits.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the profitability-like change in retained earnings with the stock of cumulative accounting losses, which measures unresolved historical distress rather than current ROA. The adjustment is active for the economically meaningful set of negative-retained-earnings firms and becomes larger with deficit severity, preventing their small market capitalizations from mechanically generating extreme value scores.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ceq, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), max( neg( re ), sub( at, at ) ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Tax-Corroborated Operating Bargain
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(txt, ABS(pi))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High EBITDA-yield firms outperform when positive tax expense relative to pretax income corroborates the operating earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: The tax channel now measures earnings corroboration rather than placing tax expense directly over market capitalization, avoiding a repackaged taxable-income yield. The minimum operator creates a bottleneck score that can be high only when both operating cheapness and tax confirmation are strong, so the distress modifier is not confined to a tiny insolvent subset.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( txt, abs( pi ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Post-Deleveraging Sales Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(lt, TS_MAX(lt, 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sales-cheap firms outperform when total liabilities have retreated materially from their recent firm-specific peak.
input_signals.reasoning: The distress channel is now distance from a historical liability maximum rather than another working-capital level or industry transformation of the archived signal. This identifies discounted firms that have completed meaningful balance-sheet repair, while industry-relative sales yield reduces structural turnover differences across sectors.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( lt, ts_max( lt, 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Funding-Gap Residual Operating Yield
input_signals.expression: IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, MAX(SUB(lct, act), SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high operating earnings relative to market value outperform after charging EBITDA for any current-liability funding gap.
input_signals.reasoning: The distress component is an operating-liquidity shortfall that directly reduces the earnings available to equity rather than a standalone leverage ratio. Because current liabilities exceed current assets for a substantial set of firms, the adjustment is economically active; industry ranking also limits distortions from sectors where negative working capital is a normal business model.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( ebitda, max( sub( lct, act ), sub( at, at ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Earnings-Instability Value Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(VOL(RATIO(pi, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book-cheap firms with unusually volatile pretax profitability relative to industry peers subsequently underperform stable cheap firms.
input_signals.reasoning: Profitability volatility captures uncertainty about whether book value can generate sustainable earnings, a distress mechanism distinct from loss levels, trends, leverage, and liquidity. Industry-standardizing volatility makes the distress term signed around zero, so book cheapness only emphasizes unusually unstable versus unusually stable firms rather than adding an independent value score.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_zscore( vol( ratio( pi, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Uncovered Maturity Residual Yield
input_signals.expression: IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, MUL(MAX(SUB(dlc, che), SUB(at, at)), RATIO(dlc, lct))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high operating earnings relative to market value outperform after charging earnings for uncovered short-term debt concentrated within current claims.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the prior denominator tweak with a nonlinear refinancing charge: only short-term debt exceeding cash is penalized, and the penalty increases with debt’s share of current liabilities. The resulting residual yield jointly measures operating cheapness and capacity to absorb a maturity wall rather than merely tracking a change in debt composition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( ebitda, mul( max( sub( dlc, che ), sub( at, at ) ), ratio( dlc, lct ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Uncompensated Earnings Instability
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(VOL(RATIO(pi, at), 5), RATIO(at, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with pretax-earnings instability that is large relative to their asset-based valuation discount subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the archived multiplicative instability signal, asset cheapness now lowers the score by compensating investors for a given amount of fundamental uncertainty. This directly targets the prior alpha disagreement: only instability not offset by a sufficiently large valuation discount receives a high trap score, while the longer window reduces volatility-estimation noise.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( vol( ratio( pi, at ), 5 ), ratio( at, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Standardized Cash-Funded Maturity Repair
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms outperform when both market-scaled cash accumulation and declining short-term debt concentration are unusually strong relative to industry peers.
input_signals.reasoning: Standardizing each leg before applying the minimum makes the cash-accumulation and maturity-repair channels commensurate. A high score now genuinely requires both improvements to be above their industry norms rather than being mechanically determined by the lower-dispersion cash term.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( che, 1 ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( neg( delta( ratio( dlc, lt ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Compensated Pretax Loss Floor
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MAX(NEG(TS_MIN(RATIO(pi, at), 5)), SUB(RATIO(at, at), RATIO(at, at))), RATIO(at, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms underperform when the magnitude of their worst recent pretax loss is not compensated by a sufficiently large asset-based valuation discount.
input_signals.reasoning: The positive-part operator assigns zero downside burden to firms whose profitability floor remains positive, eliminating the prior sign reversal for healthy firms. Asset cheapness reduces the score only when an actual loss occurred, preserving the interpretation of valuation as compensation for downside distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( max( neg( ts_min( ratio( pi, at ), 5 ) ), sub( ratio( at, at ), ratio( at, at ) ) ), ratio( at, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Residual-Cash Dividend Value
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dvc), lct), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High-dividend-yield firms outperform when operating cash flow remaining after dividends provides unusually strong coverage of current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Dividend yield alone cannot distinguish durable value from a payout that worsens distress. The soft conjunction requires both an attractive payout valuation and positive residual-cash coverage, retaining continuous variation without a hard dividend-coverage gate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( dvc, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, dvc ), lct ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Revenue Value with Liquidity Floor
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(TS_MIN(RATIO(wcap, at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-cheap firms outperform when their worst recent working-capital position remains strong relative to industry peers.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces retained-earnings change and current profitability with a downside liquidity-resilience mechanism. The standardized minimum requires both attractive revenue valuation and a strong multi-period working-capital floor, rather than re-aggregating the archived dual-cushion components.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( ts_min( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Current-Claim After-Tax Operating Yield
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at))), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), lct)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high operating earnings after positive tax expense relative to equity value and current claims subsequently outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the cash-accumulation and debt-maturity-change components of the archived repair signal. Positive tax expense is treated as a deduction from operating capacity, current liabilities are an always-active claim in the valuation base, and tax benefits cannot mechanically increase the score.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( ebitda, max( txt, sub( at, at ) ) ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), lct ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Realized Sales Growth
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(sale, 1), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oancf, 1), lct), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms outperform when market-scaled sales growth is accompanied by improving operating cash flow relative to current claims.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes current-liability reduction, so the signal no longer relies on a balance-sheet change that mechanically raises working-capital accruals. The two commensurately standardized channels test whether growth priced cheaply by the market is being realized in cash rather than merely recorded as revenue.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sale, 1 ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( oancf, 1 ), lct ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Post-Payout Liquidity Residual
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, dvc), MAX(SUB(lct, act), SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high post-dividend operating cash flow relative to market value outperform after charging for any current-liability funding gap.
input_signals.reasoning: The residual-cash dividend signal had useful cross-sectional evidence but risked sorting primarily on dividend-payer status. This integrated residual applies to payers and nonpayers, deducting both distributions and uncovered current claims before measuring the cash surplus available to equity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, dvc ), max( sub( lct, act ), sub( at, at ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Realized After-Tax Operating Value
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, lct), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms outperform when high after-tax operating yield is corroborated by strong operating-cash-flow coverage of current claims.
input_signals.reasoning: The parent signal’s strong cross-sectional slope but modest alpha suggests that accounting operating yield may not consistently translate into cash available to service near-term obligations. This construction replaces cosmetic smoothing with a commensurately standardized cash-realization condition, requiring both valuation and claim coverage to be strong.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( ebitda, max( txt, sub( at, at ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oancf, lct ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Supported Sales Expansion
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(sale, 1), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, MAX(act, lct)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms outperform when market-scaled sales growth is supported by strong operating cash generation relative to their current balance-sheet footprint.
input_signals.reasoning: Operating cash flow is used without subtracting current-liability changes because it already incorporates working-capital effects. Scaling cash flow by the larger of current assets and current liabilities provides a conservative support test, while the standardized minimum requires both inexpensive growth and cash backing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sale, 1 ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oancf, max( act, lct ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Raising Asset Rationalization
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(at, 1), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), lt), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with market-significant asset contraction outperform when the contraction is accompanied by cash accumulation relative to creditor claims.
input_signals.reasoning: The expected sign now aligns with evidence that asset contraction can predict higher returns, while cash accumulation distinguishes orderly asset monetization from destructive liquidation. A high score requires both a large asset-release yield and an improvement in liquidity relative to liabilities.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( neg( ratio( delta( at, 1 ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( che, 1 ), lt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Backed Asset Productivity Recovery
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(sale, at), 1), RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), at)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), lt), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms outperform when asset-turnover improvement is large relative to asset valuation and is accompanied by cash accumulation relative to liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This distinguishes productive rationalization from the standalone asset-contraction anomaly by requiring improved sales generated per asset rather than shrinkage itself. Cash accumulation relative to creditor claims confirms that the efficiency gain is strengthening the distress cushion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( ratio( sale, at ), 1 ), ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), at ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( che, 1 ), lt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Uncovered-Claim After-Tax Yield
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at))), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), MAX(SUB(lct, act), SUB(at, at)))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high after-tax operating earnings relative to equity value and uncovered current claims subsequently outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Penalizing all current liabilities can misclassify firms whose operating current claims are fully backed by current assets, potentially weakening the parent signal’s alpha. This integrated valuation base charges only the positive current funding gap, creating a substantively different distinction between normal operating float and genuine liquidity distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( ebitda, max( txt, sub( at, at ) ) ), add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), max( sub( lct, act ), sub( at, at ) ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Current-Claim Payout Capacity Gap
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(SUB(dvc, SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at)))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RANK(RATIO(lct, at))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms underperform when distributions are large relative to after-tax operating capacity and the current-claim burden is high.
input_signals.reasoning: The signed numerator measures payout minus after-tax operating capacity, eliminating the opposing positive dividend-yield leg and the exact negation of residual cash coverage. Current liabilities only amplify that capacity gap, while EBITDA and tax expense provide substantially broader coverage than operating cash flow.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( mul( ratio( sub( dvc, sub( ebitda, max( txt, sub( at, at ) ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), rank( ratio( lct, at ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Creditor-Funded Productivity Erosion
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(sale, at), 1), RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), at))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(lt, 1), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms underperform when asset productivity deteriorates relative to valuation while creditor claims simultaneously expand.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the previously weak cash-collapse and current-claim-concentration components. A high score instead requires both declining sales generated per asset and liability growth, identifying creditor-funded operating erosion without relying on the disputed return sign of asset contraction itself.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( neg( ratio( delta( ratio( sale, at ), 1 ), ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), at ) ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( lt, 1 ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Deteriorating Payout Capacity Trap
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvc, MAX(SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at))), SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at))), at), 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms underperform when dividends exceed positive after-tax operating capacity while that operating capacity is deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: The payout shortfall leg is zero for nonpayers with operating losses and becomes large only when actual distributions exceed positive operating support, avoiding an opposing standalone dividend-yield exposure. Requiring deterioration in after-tax operating return targets unsustainable payouts whose support is worsening rather than merely low.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( dvc, max( sub( ebitda, max( txt, sub( at, at ) ) ), sub( at, at ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( neg( delta( ratio( sub( ebitda, max( txt, sub( at, at ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dual-DuPont Valuation Trap
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at))), sale), 1), RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), sale))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(sale, at), 1), RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), at))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms underperform when both after-tax operating margin and asset turnover deteriorate substantially relative to their valuation.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the familiar liability-reduction and external-financing channels with simultaneous erosion in the two operating components of return on assets. The standardized minimum is high only when both pricing power or cost efficiency and asset productivity weaken, identifying a broad-based operating value trap rather than a single-anomaly exposure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( winsor( neg( ratio( delta( ratio( sub( ebitda, max( txt, sub( at, at ) ) ), sale ), 1 ), ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( neg( ratio( delta( ratio( sale, at ), 1 ), ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), at ) ) ), 1 ) ) )
